items.stem: Define the term “a group”.
items.answer: A vertical column of the periodic table.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a vertical column of the periodic table.

items.stem: What is the IUPAC systematic (temporary) name and symbol of the element with atomic number 101?
items.answer: unnilunium (Unu)
items.markingKey: (a) Digits 1 0 1 → un + nil + un + ium = unnilunium, symbol Unu. Its official name is mendelevium.
options: unnilunium (Unu)
ununhexium (Uuh)
unununium (Uuu)
ununtrium (Uut)

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic number.”
items.answer: Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic weight.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic weight.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the classification of elements is incorrect?
items.answer: Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic number.
items.markingKey: (d) The incorrect statement is “Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic number.” Correct form: Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic weight.
options: Eka-silicon predicted by Mendeleev was later discovered as germanium.
The position of isotopes was a problem in Mendeleev's periodic table.
Moseley showed that atomic number is a more fundamental property than atomic mass.
Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic number.

items.stem: Element 119 (ununennium, Uue) has not been characterised fully. Predict its period, group and block, and name the family it would belong to.
items.answer: Period 8, group 1, s-block; alkali metals
items.markingKey: Period 7 ends at Z = 118 (7p⁶). Z = 119 begins period 8 with 8s¹ ⇒ group 1 (1 + 1).

items.stem: Mendeleev predicted that eka-aluminium would have atomic weight about 68 and form an oxide E₂O₃. Explain how he could make such a prediction.
items.answer: From the gap below aluminium: properties of an element were taken as the average of its neighbours in the group and period; aluminium forms Al₂O₃, so its group member would form E₂O₃.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: interpolation from neighbours; 1 mark: group valency gives the formula of the oxide.

items.stem: Which of the following is a contribution of Moseley?
items.answer: showing that the frequency of X-rays emitted is related to atomic number
items.markingKey: (a) Showing that the frequency of X-rays emitted is related to atomic number is a contribution of Moseley; the others are not.
options: showing that the frequency of X-rays emitted is related to atomic number
placing some elements out of atomic-weight order to group them by properties
the law of triads
predicting the properties of eka-aluminium and eka-silicon

items.stem: An element has the IUPAC temporary name “unniloctium”. What is its atomic number and symbol?
items.answer: Z = 108; Uno
items.markingKey: Each root stands for a digit: unniloctium → 108; symbol Uno.

items.stem: In Döbereiner's triad Ca, Sr, Ba, the atomic masses of the first and third elements are 40 and 137. Predict the atomic mass of the middle element and compare it with the actual value, 88.
items.answer: 88.5; close to the actual value 88
items.markingKey: Law of triads: middle mass ≈ average of the other two = (40 + 137)/2 = 88.5, close to 88.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): In Mendeleev's table iodine (126.9) was placed after tellurium (127.6).
Reason (R): Mendeleev gave more importance to similarity in properties than to the order of atomic weights.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Iodine resembles F, Cl, Br, so he placed it with them despite the lower atomic weight.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the classification of elements is correct?
items.answer: Eka-aluminium predicted by Mendeleev was later discovered as gallium.
items.markingKey: (d) Eka-aluminium predicted by Mendeleev was later discovered as gallium. The other statements are false. Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic weight. It worked well only up to calcium. Eka-silicon is germanium; eka-aluminium is gallium.
options: Newlands' law of octaves worked well for all elements up to uranium.
Eka-silicon was later discovered as gallium.
Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic number.
Eka-aluminium predicted by Mendeleev was later discovered as gallium.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Newlands' law of octaves worked well for all elements up to uranium.”
items.answer: It worked well only up to calcium.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It worked well only up to calcium.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a contribution of Mendeleev?
items.answer: establishing atomic number as the more fundamental property
items.markingKey: (c) Establishing atomic number as the more fundamental property is a contribution of Moseley, not a contribution of Mendeleev.
options: placing some elements out of atomic-weight order to group them by properties
predicting the properties of eka-aluminium and eka-silicon
establishing atomic number as the more fundamental property
leaving gaps for undiscovered elements

items.stem: Define the term “inner transition elements”.
items.answer: The f-block elements, the lanthanoids and actinoids.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the f-block elements, the lanthanoids and actinoids.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as d-block element or s-block element: nickel, sodium, chromium, zinc.
items.answer: nickel – d-block element; sodium – s-block element; chromium – d-block element; zinc – d-block element.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: nickel – d-block element; sodium – s-block element; chromium – d-block element; zinc – d-block element.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The third period contains 18 elements.
Reason (R): Helium is placed in group 18 although its configuration is 1s².
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: The third period contains 8 elements (3s and 3p). R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

items.stem: An element has these characteristics: include metals, non-metals and metalloids; non-metallic character increases across a period. To which block of the periodic table does it belong? Give a reason.
items.answer: P-block
items.markingKey: 1 mark: p-block; 1 mark: the features include metals, non-metals and metalloids; non-metallic character increases across a period are characteristic of it.

items.stem: An element has the electronic configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p². State its period, group and block in the modern periodic table.
items.answer: Period 3, group 14, p-block
items.markingKey: Highest n = 3 ⇒ period 3; last electron enters p subshell ⇒ p-block; group 14 from the number of valence (ns + np, or ns + (n−1)d) electrons.

items.stem: Without writing the full electronic configuration, predict the period, group and block of the element with atomic number 46. Show how you decide.
items.answer: Period 5, group 10, d-block
items.markingKey: Period 4 ends at Kr (Z = 36), so Z = 46 is in period 5 (1); it is the 10th element of the period: 5s fills for 37–38, 4d for 39–48, 5p for 49–54 ⇒ group 10, d-block (1).

items.stem: Which of the following is a p-block element?
items.answer: neon
items.markingKey: (b) Neon is a p-block element; the others are not.
options: cerium
neon
iron
europium

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Helium is placed in the s-block group 2 in the periodic table.”
items.answer: Helium is placed in group 18 with the noble gases because its valence shell is completely filled.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Helium is placed in group 18 with the noble gases because its valence shell is completely filled.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the s, p, d and f blocks is correct?
items.answer: The number of elements in the fourth period is 18.
items.markingKey: (c) The number of elements in the fourth period is 18. The other statements are false. Helium is placed in group 18 with the noble gases because its valence shell is completely filled. The third period contains 8 elements (3s and 3p). d-block elements have (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns⁰⁻².
options: Helium is placed in the s-block group 2 in the periodic table.
d-block elements have the general configuration ns² np⁶.
The number of elements in the fourth period is 18.

items.stem: Hydrogen is placed in group 1 but it also resembles the halogens. Give one reason for each placement.
items.answer: Group 1: one electron in its valence shell (1s¹), forms H⁺. Halogens: needs one electron to complete its shell, forms H⁻ and diatomic molecules.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Which of the following is a d-block element?
items.answer: zinc

options: zinc
lithium
uranium
nitrogen

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between f-block and d-block on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An element has these characteristics: outer configuration (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns⁰⁻². To which block of the periodic table does it belong – f-block or d-block? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) F-block: outer configuration (n−2)f¹⁻¹⁴ (n−1)d⁰⁻¹ ns²; lanthanoids and actinoids; actinoids are radioactive. D-block: outer configuration (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns⁰⁻²; mostly form coloured ions; show variable oxidation states. (b) D-block.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: d-block; 1 mark: “outer configuration (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns⁰⁻²” is a feature of d-block.

items.stem: An element has these characteristics: placed separately at the bottom of the table; lanthanoids and actinoids. To which block of the periodic table does it belong?
items.answer: f-block
items.markingKey: (b) F-block: placed separately at the bottom of the table; lanthanoids and actinoids.
options: p-block
f-block
s-block
d-block

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a p-block element?

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The third period contains 18 elements.”
items.answer: The third period contains 8 elements (3s and 3p).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The third period contains 8 elements (3s and 3p).

items.stem: Give two differences between f-block and d-block.
items.answer: F-block: lanthanoids and actinoids; placed separately at the bottom of the table. D-block: outer configuration (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns⁰⁻²; used widely as catalysts.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. f-block – lanthanoids and actinoids; placed separately at the bottom of the table; d-block – outer configuration (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns⁰⁻²; used widely as catalysts.

items.stem: Explain the term “isoelectronic species”.
items.answer: Atoms and ions that have the same number of electrons.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: atoms and ions that have the same number of electrons.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about periodic trends is correct?
items.answer: Noble gases have large positive electron gain enthalpies.
items.markingKey: (d) Noble gases have large positive electron gain enthalpies. The other statements are false. Ionisation enthalpy generally decreases down a group as atomic size increases. B is lower than Be, because the 2p electron of B is shielded by 2s electrons and is easier to remove. Electronegativity is a dimensionless relative number (e.g. Pauling scale).

The first ionisation enthalpy of boron is higher than that of beryllium.
Ionisation enthalpy increases down a group.

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of increasing negative electron gain enthalpy (from least to most negative)?
items.answer: I < Br < F < Cl
items.markingKey: (d) I < Br < F < Cl. Cl has the most negative value; F is less negative than Cl because of strong electron repulsion in its small 2p subshell.

F < Cl < Br < I

items.stem: Which of the following statements about periodic trends is incorrect?
items.answer: An anion is smaller than its parent atom.
items.markingKey: (d) The incorrect statement is “An anion is smaller than its parent atom.” Correct form: An anion is larger because the added electron increases repulsion and the effective nuclear charge per electron falls.
options: The ionisation enthalpy of nitrogen is higher than that of oxygen.
The second ionisation enthalpy of an element is always higher than its first.
Fluorine is the most electronegative element.
An anion is smaller than its parent atom.

items.stem:
Read the data for the second-period elements and answer.
First ionisation enthalpy (kJ mol⁻¹): Li 520, Be 899, B 801, C 1086, N 1402, O 1314, F 1681, Ne 2081.
(i) What is the general trend across the period? (1 mark)
(ii) Explain why Be > B. (1 mark)
(iii) Explain why N > O. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) It increases (with exceptions). (ii) B loses a 2p electron, shielded by 2s and higher in energy. (iii) N has a stable half-filled 2p³; in O the removed electron is paired and repelled.
items.markingKey: (i) increasing nuclear charge – 1. (ii) 1. (iii) half-filled stability 1 + electron-pair repulsion in O 1.

items.stem: The first ionisation enthalpies (kJ mol⁻¹) of Na, Mg and Al are 496, 737 and 577. Explain why Mg is higher than both Na and Al.
items.answer: Mg has a higher nuclear charge than Na and a stable filled 3s² subshell; in Al the electron removed is a 3p electron, which is higher in energy and shielded by 3s, so it is removed more easily.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Mg vs Na (nuclear charge); 1 mark: Mg vs Al (3s² vs 3p¹, penetration/shielding).

items.stem: Elements A, B, C and D have first ionisation enthalpies 520, 2080, 900 and 1681 kJ mol⁻¹ and electron gain enthalpies −60, +116, positive and −328 kJ mol⁻¹. Identify (a) the most reactive metal, (b) the most reactive non-metal, (c) a noble gas, (d) a metal that forms a stable binary halide of formula MX₂. Justify each.
items.answer: (a) A (lowest IE, 520 – Li). (b) D (high IE and very negative EGE – F). (c) B (very high IE, positive EGE – Ne). (d) C (IE 900 with positive EGE – Be forms BeX₂).
items.markingKey: Identification with reason: (a) 1, (b) 1.5, (c) 1, (d) 1.5 marks.

items.stem: Which term describes the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom in its ground state?
items.answer: ionisation enthalpy
items.markingKey: (a) Ionisation enthalpy: the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom in its ground state.
options: ionisation enthalpy
the shielding effect
electron gain enthalpy
isoelectronic species

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct increasing order of first ionisation enthalpy: Rb, Cs, K, Li. Give a reason.
items.answer: Cs < Rb < K < Li
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order Cs < Rb < K < Li; 1 mark for the reason: Down group 1 atomic size increases, so the valence electron is removed more easily.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The first ionisation enthalpy of nitrogen is greater than that of oxygen.
Reason (R): Nitrogen has a half-filled, extra-stable 2p³ configuration.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Removing an electron from the stable half-filled 2p³ needs more energy; oxygen loses a paired 2p electron easily.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term “effective nuclear charge”.
items.answer: The net positive charge experienced by a valence electron after shielding by inner electrons.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the net positive charge experienced by a valence electron after shielding by inner electrons.

items.stem: Explain the term “the covalent radius”.
items.answer: Half the distance between the nuclei of two identical atoms joined by a single covalent bond.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: half the distance between the nuclei of two identical atoms joined by a single covalent bond.

items.stem: Which term describes the enthalpy change when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous atom to form an anion?

options: ionisation enthalpy
the covalent radius
electron gain enthalpy
the shielding effect

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Ionisation enthalpy increases down a group.”

items.answer: An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about periodicity of valence and chemical reactivity is correct?
items.answer: Al₂O₃ reacts with both acids and bases.

items.stem: Why do the elements of the second period (Li to F) differ from the rest of their groups in many properties?
